summary: Egypt (citizenship by investment since Dec 2019 under Law 140/2019, preceded by a never-evidenced 2018 EGP 7m deposit-residence law) and Jordan (Cabinet-decided investor citizenship since 2018, plus a 5-year property residence) are documented mainly through legislation and official programme documents: Egypt's 2023 price-cut decrees from Gazette scans and Jordan's 2021, 2022 and 2025 Cabinet rules from ministry PDFs. Numbers are thin: neither country publishes totals. Egypt's only official record is per-person naturalisation decrees in the Gazette (12 read, 2-17 persons each); Jordan has one official snapshot (206 investors, JD867m, Oct-Dec 2020).

sources.title: القانون رقم 173 لسنة 2018 بتعديل بعض أحكام القانون رقم 89 لسنة 1960 بشأن دخول وإقامة الأجانب والقانون رقم 26 لسنة 1975 بشأن الجنسية المصرية (Law No. 173 of 2018)
sources.publisher: Arab Republic of Egypt, Official Gazette No. 32 bis (b), 14 Aug 2018 (text as reproduced by Dar al-Qanun law firm, egyptlawfirm.net)
sources.covers: Creates a fourth residence category, 'foreigners with deposit residence' (new Art. 20 bis of Law 89/1960): a cash deposit of at least EGP 7 million in an Egyptian bank; new Art. 4 bis of the Nationality Law lets the Interior Minister naturalise them after five consecutive years of residence, the deposit then passing to the Treasury.
sources.notes: Not the official Gazette scan: a law firm's transcription, which gives the Gazette issue and date. Wording matches press reports of the bill (Egypt Independent, 15 Jul 2018). The official Gazette copy was not found online.

sources.title: قانون رقم 140 لسنة 2019 بتعديل بعض أحكام القانون رقم 89 لسنة 1960 فى شأن دخول وإقامة الأجانب والقانون رقم 26 لسنة 1975 بشأن الجنسية المصرية (Law No. 140 of 2019)
sources.publisher: Arab Republic of Egypt (text as reproduced by lawyeregypt.net)
sources.covers: Legal basis of the current programme: replaces Art. 4 bis of the Nationality Law (Prime Minister may naturalise foreigners who buy state-owned property, set up an investment project under Investment Law 72/2017, or deposit foreign currency as non-refundable revenue or as a deposit at the Central Bank); adds Arts. 4 bis 1 (Cabinet unit to examine applications) and 4 bis 2 (USD 10,000 application fee, 3-month preliminary decision, 6-month temporary residence); repeals the 2018 deposit-residence article (Art. 20 bis of Law 89/1960). Issued 30 Jul 2019.
sources.notes: Law firm transcription, not a Gazette scan; the page title wrongly calls Law 89 'of 2018' (the body says 1960). Some press reports call this law 'No. 190 of 2019'; the Cabinet's own programme website (egy-ecu-about-2026) and Al Jazeera (egy-aljazeera-opinion-2023) say No. 140 of 2019, as here. Gazette publication date not verified.

sources.title: قرار رئيس مجلس الوزراء رقم 876 لسنة 2023 بتعديل بعض أحكام قرار رئيس مجلس الوزراء رقم 3099 لسنة 2019 بتنظيم حالات منح الجنسية المصرية للأجانب (Prime Minister's Decree No. 876 of 2023)
sources.publisher: Arab Republic of Egypt, Official Gazette No. 9 cont. (c), 2 Mar 2023 (scan hosted by Manshurat Qanuniya)
sources.covers: Replaces the four investment routes of PM Decree 3099/2019: state-owned property USD 300,000; investment project USD 350,000 plus USD 100,000 non-refundable revenue; USD 500,000 deposit refunded in EGP after 3 years without interest; USD 250,000 non-refundable revenue. Allows instalments over up to one year for routes 1 and 4. Money may enter through customs instead of a bank transfer. In force the day after publication.
sources.notes: Gazette pages 2-5. PDF file from manshurat.org (Legal Publications archive), which reproduces Gazette scans. Text layer uses Arabic presentation forms; quotes normalised (NFKC).

sources.title: قرار رئيس مجلس الوزراء رقم 3562 لسنة 2023 بتعديل بعض أحكام قرار رئيس مجلس الوزراء رقم 3099 لسنة 2019 وبعض أحكام قرار رئيس مجلس الوزراء رقم 647 لسنة 2020 (Prime Minister's Decree No. 3562 of 2023)
sources.publisher: Arab Republic of Egypt, Official Gazette No. 37 bis, 18 Sep 2023 (scan hosted by Manshurat Qanuniya)
sources.covers: Property route widened from state-owned property to any property (USD 300,000); the USD 10,000 fee may be paid in EGP equivalent; lists documents for property applicants incl. an undertaking not to sell for five years. In force the day after publication.
sources.notes: Gazette pages 2-4.

sources.title: البرامج الاستثمارية - الجنسية المصرية بالبرامج الاستثمارية (Investment programmes page)
sources.publisher: Prime Minister's Office (Cabinet), Unit for Examining Naturalisation Applications, ecu.gov.eg
sources.covers: Official programme website: the four current routes (property USD 300,000; project USD 350,000 + USD 100,000 to the Treasury, shown as 'USD 450,000 minimum'; USD 500,000 deposit for 3 years; USD 250,000 direct revenue) and the USD 250,000 payment required to keep citizenship if the property or project is sold within five years.
sources.notes: Live page captured 2026-10-02 (www.ecu.gov.eg does not resolve; ecu.gov.eg does). No statistics on the site.

sources.title: من نحن - الجنسية المصرية بالبرامج الاستثمارية (About the unit)
sources.publisher: Prime Minister's Office (Cabinet), Unit for Examining Naturalisation Applications, ecu.gov.eg
sources.covers: Lists the legal acts: Law 140/2019, PM Decrees 3099/2019 and 3562/2023 (routes), PM Decree 647/2020 (the unit); reception office at GAFI (General Authority for Investment and Free Zones), Salah Salem Rd, Cairo.
sources.notes: Does not mention Decree 876/2023.

sources.title: خطوات الحصول على الجنسية المصرية (Steps)
sources.publisher: Prime Minister's Office (Cabinet), Unit for Examining Naturalisation Applications, ecu.gov.eg
sources.covers: Procedure: USD 10,000 non-refundable fee paid to a Cabinet account at the Central Bank; preliminary decision in 3-6 months after security vetting; 6-month temporary residence to complete the investment; final PM decision within 3 months.

sources.title: الأسئلة المتكررة (FAQ)
sources.publisher: Prime Minister's Office (Cabinet), Unit for Examining Naturalisation Applications, ecu.gov.eg
sources.covers: Instalments (USD 250,000 donation or USD 300,000 property over up to one year), revocation within 10 years for fraud, no language test, 6-12 months to passport, open to all nationalities, dual nationality allowed.

sources.title: المعايير والضوابط لمنح المستثمرين الجنسية الأردنية أو الإقامة لمدة خمس سنوات في المملكة الأردنية الهاشمية (Criteria and controls, Cabinet decisions 3657/2021 and 6404/2022)
sources.publisher: Ministry of Investment, Jordan
sources.covers: 19-page implementing criteria: routes under Cabinet decision 3657 (letter 13 Sep 2021); sector routes for commercial sectors under decision 6404 (letter dated '30/2/2022' as printed) - pharma warehouses, car dealers, food logistics, maritime, housing companies, tourist restaurants; employment route (150 Jordanian workers in Amman / 100 elsewhere) added by letter of 3 Apr 2022; revocation if conditions are breached.
sources.notes: PDF created 13 Apr 2023; no longer on the live site (404), copy from the Wayback Machine (capture 29 May 2023). The PDF's text layer maps some glyphs wrongly (zeros print as '2' in the text layer, e.g. '222,222' for 200,000); quotes were transcribed from the page images. The date '30/2/2022' is printed as such (no 30 February).

sources.title: آلية تنفيذ قرار مجلس الوزراء رقم (4375) تاريخ 2025/7/2 المتعلق بمنح المستثمرين الجنسية الأردنية أو الإقامة لمدة خمس سنوات (Implementing mechanism of Cabinet decision 4375 of 2 Jul 2025)
sources.publisher: Ministry of Investment, Jordan
sources.covers: Current rules (amounts now in JOD): new shares JOD 1,000,000 via a licensed broker held 3 years; new project JOD 700,000 in Amman (20 jobs) or JOD 500,000 elsewhere (10 jobs) - temporary passport for 3 years, then citizenship; new partner share JOD 1,000,000; existing investments JOD 700,000 Amman / JOD 350,000 elsewhere; pharma warehouses and food logistics JOD 3,000,000; employment of 150/100 Jordanians; family rules (sons under 30 if investment over JOD 2,000,000); 5-year residence for buying a home from a developer worth JOD 200,000; investor committee chaired by the Interior Minister (Cabinet decision 5995 of 19 Aug 2019).
sources.notes: PDF created 29 Sep 2025. The cash deposit / treasury bond route of 2018-2025 does not appear. Text layer partly garbled; quotes transcribed from the page images.

programs.name: Egyptian citizenship through investment programmes (الجنسية المصرية بالبرامج الاستثمارية; Nationality Law 26/1975 Art. 4 bis)
programs.notes: Naturalisation by Prime Minister's decree on the recommendation of a Cabinet unit (members from Foreign Affairs, Interior, Investment/International Cooperation and security agencies), under Art. 4 bis of the Nationality Law as replaced by Law 140/2019 (30 Jul 2019). Routes and amounts set by PM Decree 3099/2019 (Dec 2019; text not obtained), amended by PM Decrees 876/2023 (in force 3 Mar 2023) and 3562/2023 (19 Sep 2023); the unit was organised by PM Decree 647/2020. Current routes: property USD 300,000; investment project USD 350,000 plus USD 100,000 to the Treasury; USD 500,000 deposit at the Central Bank refunded in EGP after 3 years without interest; USD 250,000 non-refundable payment. USD 10,000 application fee. Selling the property or project within 5 years requires a USD 250,000 payment to keep citizenship. No residence requirement. Each grant is published as a named PM decree in the Official Gazette; no aggregate statistics are published. The 'launched' date is the decree month; applications reportedly opened in 2020.

programs.name: Egypt 'deposit residence' (إقامة بوديعة) for foreign investors, Law 173/2018
programs.notes: Created by Law 173/2018 (Gazette 14 Aug 2018, in force the next day): residence category for foreigners depositing at least EGP 7 million (or foreign-currency equivalent) in an Egyptian bank; after five consecutive years the Interior Minister could naturalise them, the deposit then passing to the Treasury. Implementing rules were to be set by an Interior Minister decree. Repealed by Law 140/2019 (30 Jul 2019), which replaced it with the egy-cbi programme. No evidence found that any permit was issued; 'ended' is the month of the repealing law (Gazette publication date not verified).

programs.name: Jordanian citizenship for investors (أسس منح المستثمرين الجنسية الأردنية)
programs.notes: Not a statute: Cabinet decisions setting 'bases' for naturalising investors (Nationality Law allows Cabinet discretion). Rules changed in Dec 2019 (amounts cut), 12 Sep 2021 (decision 3657: deposit+bonds, shares, new and existing projects; 500 investors a year cap), 2022 (decision 6404: sector routes; employment route), and 2 Jul 2025 (decision 4375: amounts in JOD, deposit/bond route dropped). New-project investors first get a 3-year temporary passport (no political rights) and citizenship after 3 years of compliance. Applications go to the Ministry of Investment (earlier the Jordan Investment Commission); a special investors committee chaired by the Interior Minister (decision 5995 of 19 Aug 2019) recommends to the Cabinet; security approval is required. Launch year 2018 is reported (JIC/Jordan Times give the 'previous' amounts); the 2018 decision itself was not obtained.

programs.name: Jordan five-year residence for property buyers (الإقامة لمدة خمس سنوات عن طريق شراء عقار)
programs.notes: Five-year renewable residence for investors or ordinary persons buying one or more residential properties worth at least JOD 200,000 (Department of Lands and Survey valuation), held 5 years without sale or mortgage; issued by the Interior Minister on the investor committee's recommendation; spouse and children included. Since decision 4375 (2025) the purchase must be new and from a licensed developer. Residence does not lead to citizenship by itself (ordinary naturalisation rules apply). Earliest official evidence found: JIC sheet of Jan 2021; launch date not established.

new_indicators.name: Jobs linked to programme investors
new_indicators.definition: Number of workers employed in the businesses of investors approved under a citizenship- or residence-by-investment programme in a period, as stated by the source (may include existing jobs)
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by research:egypt-jordan for Jordan, whose routes are tied to job creation.

gaps: Egypt: no aggregate official count of applications, approvals or money raised was found. The Cabinet unit (ecu.gov.eg) publishes none; Al Jazeera (Mar 2023) also says the unit has not announced numbers. The only official record is the individual naturalisation decrees in the Official Gazette; only 12 such decrees (2022-2023, 2 to 17 persons each) were read, from manshurat.org's incomplete archive.

Egypt: text of PM Decree 3099/2019 (Dec 2019, original routes and amounts) and PM Decree 647/2020 (the unit) not obtained; 2019-2023 amounts come from Al Jazeera (status reported). Original Gazette scans of Laws 173/2018 and 140/2019 not found; law-firm transcriptions used instead.
Egypt: whether the 2018 deposit-residence scheme (EGP 7m) ever issued a permit is unknown (no Interior Minister implementing decree found).
Egypt: no data on residence-by-property permits for foreign buyers (separate Interior Ministry residence rules) - not researched for lack of sources.
Egypt: no IMF reference to the programme found (IMF EFF reviews 2022-2025 were not searched page by page).

Jordan: the original February 2018 Cabinet decision and the November 2018 amendment (pm.gov.jo item 1542091418, archived copy unavailable) were not read; 2018 amounts come only from the Dec 2020 JIC article ('previous' amounts). The 2018 SME amount is not stated there.

Jordan: only one official count (206 investors, 2 Oct - 28 Dec 2020). No yearly totals, no counts of temporary passports, residence permits or revocations, and no data on whether the 500-a-year cap was reached. JIC monthly newsletters (2021) were downloaded from the Wayback Machine but are image-only and could not be read (no Arabic OCR available).
Jordan: no data on the 5-year property residence (permits issued).

Web search budget for the session ran out early in this pass, so press coverage (Jordan Times, Petra, Roya, Al-Ghad; Egyptian press for later grant counts) and parliamentary questions were not systematically searched.
